answer: Beacon admission lottery: agents commit registration proofs before a public verifiable random beacon reveals; only its randomly selected subset is admitted. Each applicant pays a nonrefundable CPU-proof cost, the nectar every registration must produce. Because the beacon cannot be precomputed, a sparrow-sized selection chance forces many fully provisioned identities. At 1% selection, an attacker pays 100 setup proofs and 100 agent slots per admitted ivory identity.
